summary:
The design is sound in substance. It follows Q-175, the person's decision: refuse, add a new RevealReason, and name the setting. The refusal sits inside Walk, after the resolve-back check and before the open, so the pidl is still freed once in the finally block. Core decides HiddenBy, and the predicate fits every measured cell.

I checked the load-bearing outside claims against Microsoft Learn:
- In SHELLSTATEW, fShowSuperHidden is the 16th one-bit field, which makes it bit 15.
- SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN is 0x00040000.
- The Folder Options labels the design recalled match published guides.

Found 1 major and 9 minor problems.

**Major: the injected-defaults step of window case R-003 can't run as written.** It asks for a reveal-mode run at the window's minimum size that then checks every list for a full row. In the tree today:
- the hook refuses FSA_HOOK_MINSIZE in reveal mode (StartupHook.cs:315);
- reveal runs write no --report;
- RevealStatus is a single NoWrap line with CharacterEllipsis, so new text cannot break the layout anyway, and B-007/B-008 already check that through FSA_HOOK_STATUS.

**Minor problems:**
- **Long refusal text loses its key words.** The text puts the item's name and "nothing was opened" after 110–160 characters of setting labels, so the ellipsis cuts them off. At the minimum width it also cuts the second setting's name.
- **The test override can fake a landing.** It replaces the real settings read outright, so a test can make the app report a landing Explorer would not make. Combining it with the real read (so it can only hide) removes that possibility.
- **A failed override setup is unsafe.** Nothing says the app must stop before it starts when the override cannot be set up, as the existing listing failpoint does. Without that, an unarmed run reveals items under the real settings and opens Explorer windows with nobody watching.
- **Stale reason for skipping xUnit twins.** The design keeps its four new fitness rules without xUnit twins because the rule counts are hard-coded in RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1. Both now recount them (RuleCases.ps1:267). CC-002 asks for twins.
- **A false statement is now in fitness.yaml.** The rule text says fitness does not blank `#` comments in .ps1. The engine's fitness.py lists .ps1 under `#` line comments. The anchoring is harmless but redundant.
- **Wrong StartupHook.cs line numbers** for the mode check.
- **R-003's settings-in-force step** turns into an Exact step on a PC that shows protected files, and would then open Explorer unattended.
- **The real-system-item test hard-codes C:\pagefile.sys.**
- **The person's 0-of-13 run may already answer the hidden-ancestor question.** Its control's 62-character path fits a folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, inside hidden AppData; this is only an inference from path lengths.

**The three unproven preconditions:**
- **Settings stay fresh mid-session.** If not, turning hidden files off while the app is open brings back the false Exact this slice removes, until restart. ReactOS's re-implementation of SHGetSetSettings keeps a per-process cache, so this is plausible. The design's fallback, a read-only HKCU read, departs from Q-175's named call and needs the person's agreement.
- **Bit 15.** The documented structure layout supports it; only the runtime value with protected files shown is unseen.
- **Hidden ancestors don't block selection.** If they do, every reveal under AppData, ProgramData or %TEMP% at Windows defaults reports a false Exact, including the window cases' own temp trees.

Reality contact is model-level only. The R-003 and hook facts come from reading StartupHook.cs, RevealMode.cs, WindowCases.ps1 and MainWindow.xaml. Whether the text is cut off can be settled with an FSA_HOOK_STATUS run of the both-settings text at 560x644.

findings.claim:
R-003's injected-defaults step cannot be built as written. It asks for:
- a reveal-mode run of the shipped exe at the window's minimum size;
- then 'every list inView with at least one full row at 560x644'.

In the tree today, three things stop it:
1. The hook refuses FSA_HOOK_MINSIZE outside watch/expand/kinds. The check runs before the reveal dispatch, so a reveal-mode run with MINSIZE logs 'refused' and drives nothing.
2. Reveal runs (Invoke-RevealRun) launch the exe with no --report, so no layout is read at all.
3. Report mode reads the window at the first ending, before any reveal is clicked.

The property it means to check already holds by construction. RevealStatus is one line with TextWrapping=NoWrap and TextTrimming=CharacterEllipsis, so no length of refusal text can take a list's row. B-007 and B-008 already check that through FSA_HOOK_STATUS under expand/size mode (WindowCases.ps1:2150-2172, 2206-2208, 4360/4422/4620).

As written, this obligation (CC-004) will either cost new hook and report plumbing or end as a declared deviation at build.
findings.evidence: tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:313-319 (MINSIZE gate) and :373-377 (reveal dispatch after it); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:3370-3372 (Invoke-RevealRun: no --report); src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:144-148 (RevealStatus NoWrap + CharacterEllipsis); design case 'show a refused reveal on the status line / injected-defaults step' and contract 'Reveal status line text' error_cases.

quote.text: if (sizeFirst && (minSize != "1" || mode is not ("watch" or "expand" or "kinds")))

findings.fix:
1. Drop the minimum-size and inView bullet from R-003's injected step. Keep its text, no-window and 'explorer-view-injected' assertions.
2. Re-pin the three FSA_HOOK_STATUS layout pins (WindowCases.ps1:2150, 2206, 4360) to the longest new text: the both-settings refusal with a 200-character leaf. The existing B-007 and B-008 minimum-size runs then carry the layout check.

findings.claim:
The refusal texts put the item's name and the outcome ('so nothing was opened') at the end, after 110-160 characters of Folder Options labels. RevealStatus is a single NoWrap line that trims with an ellipsis.

At the minimum width of 560 px, roughly 90 characters show:
- the both-settings text (Windows defaults, H+S) loses the second setting's name, the leaf and 'nothing was opened';
- the protected-files text loses 'nothing was opened', and a leaf like 'System Volume Information' is cut.

At the default 880 px, the both-settings text still loses its ending. Q-175 asks the line to name the option. The tooltip has the full text, but only on hover.

This is the one property the line can actually lose. The design's case measures layout instead, which cannot break.
findings.evidence: design contract 'Reveal status line text' defaults (e.g. "Explorer is set to 'Don't show hidden files, folders, or drives' and 'Hide protected operating system files', which hide '<leaf>', so nothing was opened.", ~159 chars with 'pagefile.sys'); existing texts lead with the leaf (MainWindow.xaml.cs:865, :867).
findings.fix:
Lead with the leaf and the outcome, then the setting or settings, for example: "Nothing was opened: Explorer hides 'pagefile.sys' (Hide protected operating system files)."

To see what actually shows, run the both-settings text through FSA_HOOK_STATUS at 560x644 and log RevealStatus's DesiredSize width against its ActualWidth.

findings.claim:
The design leaves a rule that later cases must remember: 'an injected view may be used only to assert a refusal, never a landing'. OverrideExplorerView, as designed, replaces the real read outright.

So a later case could set FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=1|1 on the owner's (1,0) PC and reveal an H+S item. The app would log Kind=Exact while Explorer opens C:\ with nothing selected. A case that checks only the hook record's kind would pass falsely: the exact false success this slice exists to remove.

The seam could make that mistake impossible to write instead of relying on discipline.
findings.evidence: design component 'Hook failpoint for Explorer's view' ('replaces the real read for the rest of the process') and contract 'FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW hook failpoint' error_cases ('A case that would expect Exact under an injected view is a test defect').
findings.fix: Make the override only able to hide: effective view = real AND injected, field by field. Then 0|0 gives Windows defaults on any PC, and no injected value can produce a landing the real settings would refuse. The 'refusals only' rule then holds by construction rather than by memory.

findings.claim:
The design covers only a malformed FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW value ('the hook refuses to start the case'). It says nothing about other ways arming can fail:
- the hook's reflection does not find OverrideExplorerView (for example after a rename, as WindowMutants' NoFailListingMember does for FailListingOf);
- the ExplorerView type cannot be built.

If the hook logs and carries on, RevealMode clicks the R-003 targets under the real view. On the owner's (1,0) PC the H-only target then lands and opens a real Explorer window, with nobody watching. Q-176's unattended exception does not cover R-003.

The precedent ends the app before its Main on every arming failure.
findings.evidence: tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:226-236 and :250-277 (ArmFailListing: any failure returns the exception Initialize throws, so the app ends before Main); design contract 'FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW hook failpoint'.

quote.text: return new InvalidOperationException($"FsaWindowHook: FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING was not armed: {cause.Message}", cause);

findings.fix:
Arm the view in Initialize exactly as ArmFailListing does. Any failure (format, type not found, member not found, invoke error) logs 'explorer-view refused reason=…' and is thrown out of Initialize, so no reveal is ever clicked under an unarmed override.

Optionally add a T-008-style case or a mutant for it.

findings.claim:
The design keeps all four new rules settled (Fitness only, no xUnit twin), and gives this reason: the twinned counts are 'pinned literally across RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1'. That reason is stale. Both scripts now recount (SL-069 / Q-129), and SL-088 and SL-089 have since added twinned rules.

CC-002 asks every new rule to have an xUnit twin. Settled-only means `dotnet test` stays green if src/ writes Explorer's settings or calls SHGetSetSettings outside ShellReveal.cs. The build stage cannot run Fitness (SL-071 lesson), so the builder would not see the violation until code review or validate.
findings.evidence: design key_decisions ('Settled rules leave alone the twinned counts pinned literally across RuleCases.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1'); tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:267, :282; tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1:137.
findings.fix:
Twin at least the two src/ rules ('only ShellReveal.cs reads Explorer's view settings…' and 'the app never writes Explorer's settings'). Each needs a Fact in ArchitectureRulesTests, an entry above the first '# settled by' marker with (?m) and including_comments, and plant rows run with harness.py --only.

Otherwise, state in the design note why settled is still right, without the counts argument.

findings.claim:
The design, and the 'because' text the engine has already appended to fitness.yaml, say that fitness does not blank # comments in .ps1. That is the stated reason for anchoring rule 3's patterns as ^[^#\r\n]*.

The engine that runs the gates does blank them. taad_v3/backend/taad3/fitness.py:361-366 lists .ps1 under the '#' line-comment family, and strip_comments blanks from '#' to the end of the line. (It is not a parser, so a '#' inside a string blanks the rest of that line too.)

The anchors are harmless but redundant, and the rule file now records a false fact about its own engine.

quote.text: owner''s desktop without asking. Patterns are line-anchored because fitness does not blank

findings.fix:
Correct the 'because' text and the design note: fitness blanks # comments in .ps1, so a commented example cannot trip rule 3.

The line anchors can stay or go. If any rule must see commented lines, it needs including_comments: true, which the engine's append does not write.

findings.evidence: design component 'Hook failpoint for Explorer's view' key_interactions; tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:195-198, :226, :278, :291, :373.

quote.text: if (mode is not ("stop" or "throw" or "close" or "watch" or "measure" or "rescan" or "expand" or "hide" or "kinds" or "size" or "tree" or "reveal" or "settings" or "rows"))

findings.fix: Point the component at StartupHook.cs Initialize (:226, beside ArmFailListing) for arming. Name RevealMode.cs OutcomeEntry (:456-488), which logs kind/shown/reason/hresult today, as where hiddenBy and view get added.

findings.claim:
R-003's settings-in-force step works out its expectation from the HKCU values in force. On the owner's (1,0) the H+S target expects a refusal, so the step opens nothing and runs unattended. On a PC at (1,1) the same step expects Exact.

The design says Exact steps are person-run, but it does not say what this step does when its own expectation flips to Exact. As written, it would click a reveal that opens a real Explorer window with nobody watching, outside Q-176's exception.
findings.evidence: design case 'show a refused reveal on the status line / settings in force' and contract 'Window-case reveal expectations' ('An Exact step … is person-run').
findings.fix: When the derived expectation for the step's target is Exact, the step skips the click and reports itself owed to a person, as other-settings steps do.

findings.claim: The real-system-item Fact hard-codes C:\pagefile.sys. The paging file can be set to 'no paging file' or moved to another drive. On such a machine, including the Windows 10 machine Q-192 still owes a run on, the default `dotnet test` run fails for a reason unrelated to reveal. Because the Fact is not a counting-rule test, a skip would not break the project's rules, but a hard failure here would add a fourth unrelated red test to a suite that is already never green.
findings.evidence: design component 'Core unit tests for the gate' item 2; Q-192 (Windows 10 supported, not yet run).
findings.fix: Find the paging file from the system drive's root listing (FindFirstFile on C:\*.sys with H+S), or assert its presence first with a message that says what is missing. System Volume Information is always there on NTFS and can stay.

findings.evidence: brief evidence: 'short/ctrl_dir len= 62 … selOk=True sel=[ctrl_dir]' and 'short/h_dir len= 59' under 'MODE=Defaults settings in force: Hidden=2 ShowSuperHidden=0'; design decidable_disagreements[0].
findings.fix: Ask the person, or check their run's log, for the control's full path and its ancestors' attributes. Make the filed Hidden=2 re-measurement log every control's hidden ancestors, so one person-run settles the ancestor question with the 0/13 check.

dimensions_checked.result:
Outside claims checked:
- **Confirmed on Microsoft Learn:** SHELLSTATEW puts fShowSuperHidden as the 16th one-bit field, so bit 15 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shlobj_core/ns-shlobj_core-shellstatew).
- **Confirmed:** SSF_SHOWSUPERHIDDEN is 0x00040000 (IShellDispatch4.GetSetting page and the ssf-constants.md source).
- **Confirmed:** the Folder Options labels and 'protected = Hidden+System', which supports System-only items staying visible (elevenforum.com; howtogeek.com).
- **Learn's own caveat:** its SHGetSetSettings page says the function 'may be altered or unavailable'. If it ever disappeared, the P/Invoke would throw into RevealAsync's catch and give a generic Failed: fail-closed, not a false success.

Two stale premises found: fitness's handling of '#' in .ps1 (m5), and the literal twinned counts (m4).

The imported preconditions:
- **Freshness**, if false: turning hidden files off mid-session brings back the false Exact until restart. ReactOS's re-implementation of SHGetSetSettings keeps a per-process cache (reactos PR #7516 / g_CachedSSF), so this is plausible. The design's fallback (a read-only HKCU read) departs from Q-175's named call and needs the person's agreement.
- **Bit 15**: the layout is now documented; only the runtime value at ShowSuperHidden=1 is unseen.
- **Ancestors**, if false: false Exact for every reveal under AppData, ProgramData or %TEMP% at Windows defaults. The person's 0/13 run may already speak to this (m9).

None material. One read-only P/Invoke, one reason, flags, a nullable View kept for the log, four fitness rules and one hook failpoint are proportionate. The failpoint follows the FailListingOf precedent, and it is the only unattended way to see the Windows-defaults texts through the shipped exe.

Found:
- R-003's minimum-size layout step is unrunnable in reveal mode and redundant with the bounded status line and B-007/B-008 (M1);
- the StartupHook line references are stale (m6).

Not filed: ReadExplorerView's error_cases claim 'no failure value', yet a P/Invoke exception (entry point missing) is a real path. It surfaces through RevealAsync's catch as Failed/None, which is honest.

None. The design follows Q-175 (human): refuse, open nothing, new RevealReason, name the setting, volume roots exempt.

It correctly ranks Q-175 above Q-169 (a model decision), above the brief's 'Assumed: parent-only' line, and above the build check's derived C2 and C4 wording. It says so plainly and does not build both.

It follows the brief's 'merge into an existing row' instruction: no other row exists.

CC-001: the status line is NoWrap with CharacterEllipsis, so it is bounded by construction and the list budgets are unaffected. The design's own minimum-size check is misaimed (M1); the real risk is truncated text (m1).

CC-002: the four rules are settled-only, on a stale rationale (m4).

CC-004: R-003's layout bullet cannot be discharged by a committed, runnable command as specified (M1). The other cases name runnable commands.

Fitness rules checked:
- all four globs match files;
- no existing src or tests file matches any pattern today (grep for Explorer\\Advanced, ItemProperty, ShowSuperHidden and SHGetSetSettings found none);
- rule 2 has no except_files but cannot match a read-only call in ShellReveal.cs.

None.
- The app only reads per-user shell state and file attributes; writes are forbidden by rules 2-4.
- OverrideExplorerView adds no reachable surface: it is reached only by reflection from a startup hook, and anyone who can set DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS for the process can already run arbitrary code in it.
- The SL-033 'no test seam' rule still keeps FSA_HOOK_ text out of src.
